keyVerseText: And by the river upon the bank thereof, on this side and on that side, shall grow all trees for meat, whose leaf shall not fade, neither shall the fruit thereof be consumed: it shall bring forth new fruit according to his months, because their waters they issued out of the sanctuary: and the fruit thereof shall be for meat, and the leaf thereof for medicine. shall grow: Heb. shall come up new: or, principal for medicine: or, for bruises and sores
rootMeaning: The Hebrew noun תְּרוּפָה (tᵉrûwphâh) derives from the root רוּף (rûwph), which primarily means 'to tremble' or 'to triturate,' suggesting a process of grinding or agitation. This root is related to רָפָא, meaning 'to heal,' indicating that תְּרוּפָה carries the idea of something prepared or processed to bring about healing. Thus, beyond the simple English term 'medicine,' the root implies a careful preparation or treatment aimed at restoration and health.
usageInScripture: The word תְּרוּפָה occurs only once in the Hebrew Bible, specifically in Ezekiel 47:12. It is translated as 'medicine' or 'remedy,' highlighting its role as a healing agent. The singular occurrence suggests a specialized usage, emphasizing the curative properties of the leaves of the trees described in this prophetic vision. This limited but focused use underscores the concept of divine provision for physical healing through natural means.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding תְּרוּפָה as a divinely linked remedy enriches our appreciation of God's provision for holistic restoration—both physical and spiritual. The root meaning, which involves a process of preparation or agitation, reflects the intentional care God takes in providing healing. This aligns with the biblical theme of God as the ultimate healer, whose sanctuary waters bring life and renewal. For the Christian faith, it points forward to Christ, the Great Physician, who not only heals bodily afflictions but also restores the soul. The word thus invites believers to trust in God's sustaining grace and restorative power.
keyVerseReflection: Ezekiel 47:12 describes trees growing along the riverbank whose leaves serve as תְּרוּפָה, or medicine, for the people. The verse emphasizes that these leaves will not fade and their fruit will not be consumed, symbolizing perpetual healing and sustenance. The use of תְּרוּפָה here highlights the life-giving and restorative nature of God's provision flowing from the sanctuary, assuring believers that God’s healing power is both enduring and accessible.
